findings.description: Nit: The exact eight-step rehydration order is not on the plan's declared normative surface. contracts/README.md says the behavioral contract is the skill-workflow delta plus design.md D1–D4, but the numbered eight-step sequence lives only in the separate Rehydration Algorithm section (design.md:39-46). Decision D3 (design.md:22-25) collapses roadmap.yaml/cycle-ledger validation into checkpoint verification and never names step 8 (Rebuild projections). The OpenSpec scenario Fresh supervisor session resumes active work (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:23-28) only requires locator use, checkpoint-before-loop-state, and advisory-after-authoritative. Consequence: a future editor can drop steps 2 or 8 from the guide while remaining scenario-green under the contracts pointer, recreating the projection/authority ambiguity this change exists to prevent.
findings.resolution: Update contracts/README.md to cite the Rehydration Algorithm (or an equivalently numbered D-decision) as normative; tighten D3 so it names all eight steps; and extend the Fresh supervisor session scenario with AND clauses for roadmap definition before checkpoint verification and projection rebuild last.

findings.description: Nit: proposal.md What Changes requires documenting each class's mutation boundary, but design.md D1 (line 11), the inventory requirement in specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:5, and Success Criteria (proposal.md:67) all omit that field and list only path, holder/scope, writer, authority, consumers, and missing/stale behavior. Consequence: an implementer following the proposal bullet will add a column the structural contract (tasks.md 1.1 required ownership fields / D1) does not expect, or an implementer following D1/spec will omit a field the proposal still claims is in scope.
findings.resolution: Either remove mutation boundary from proposal.md What Changes, or add it to design.md D1, the inventory SHALL clause, Success Criteria, and the task 1.1/2.1 ownership-field coverage so all four surfaces agree.

findings.description: Nit: proposal.md Impact lists the guide, documentation index, six skill sources, runtime mirrors, focused tests, and the skill-workflow capability, but work-packages.yaml locks.files/write_allow also include skills/pyproject.toml (task 1.3 CI registration) and docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md (D5 derived decision index). Consequence: reviewers comparing the proposal declaration to the package allowlist see an unexplained scope expansion, and a later archive/diff audit cannot tell those two writes were intentional plan scope.
findings.resolution: Add skills/pyproject.toml and the regenerated docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md projection to proposal.md Impact (and a brief What Changes bullet for CI registration of the structural suite).

findings.description: Single sequential package wp-state-artifacts-docs with depends_on: [] is the right decomposition: guide prose, six canonical skill sources, generated mirrors, and one structural test module share one semantic drift boundary, with an explicit write_allow and denies on agent-coordinator and apps.
findings.resolution: No action; keep the single-package DAG and allowlist.

findings.description: Missing-canonical-state behavior is fail-loud and non-synthesizing: Canonical state is missing requires reporting degraded/inconsistent state and forbids reconstructing authoritative phase state from handoff, learning log, phase record, or queue, matching design.md D3 and the ri-09 motivation in proposal.md.
findings.resolution: No action; retain the degrade-don't-invent rule.

findings.description: Non-goals and contracts/README.md correctly exclude artifact schema, runtime state machine, coordinator API, persistence, and rename/migration work, so the documentation-only change cannot be misread as authorizing behavioral rewrites.
findings.resolution: No action; keep runtime and schema changes out of scope.

findings.description: Advisory-versus-authoritative conflicts are observable by requirement: Advisory state conflicts with authoritative state requires the authoritative record to win and the conflict to be reported rather than silently merged, giving operators a detectable signal when handoffs or learnings disagree with loop/checkpoint state.
findings.resolution: No action; keep conflict reporting as a required outcome.
